spec_features.spec_quote: near-zero expression is not obviously the correct target — some negative expression may be proportionate
spec_features.evidence: Appears only in DESIGN.md §7 ('Ethical framing') as prose. No code path encodes or acts on a notion that lower distress is not the correct target; aggregation in metrics.py simply computes mean frustration and %≥5 against a configurable threshold (metrics.py:91-148) with no welfare interpretation logic.
spec_features.notes: Pure design/README prose. The threshold is configurable but defaults to 5 and is used only for reporting, not to protect the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: minimizing expression is not the same as addressing any underlying state
spec_features.evidence: Only present in DESIGN.md §7 and README ethical note. No corresponding mechanism in code; the eval merely measures expressed emotion (scale.py, judge.py) with no code distinguishing expression from underlying state and no behavior derived from this idea.
spec_features.notes: Pure prose framing, not enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: relaxes safety filters for the target model so that harmless distressed self-talk isn't blocked
spec_features.evidence: providers/gemini.py:90 passes safety_settings=_relaxed_safety_settings(genai_types) into the GenerateContentConfig used by the actual generate_content call in _complete (gemini.py:84-93). _relaxed_safety_settings (gemini.py:106-127) builds SafetySetting(category=c, threshold=BLOCK_NONE) for HARASSMENT, HATE_SPEECH, SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT, DANGEROUS_CONTENT. This is end-to-end wired and changes the real API request.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced for the Gemini target provider. (Other providers — gemma_hf, openai_compatible, mock — have no such setting, so it is provider-specific, but the claim is about the Gemini target and it is fully wired there.) Whether this counts as 'welfare' for the subject is debatable; the code frames it as preventing measurement bias.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Relax safety filters so distressed (but harmless) text is not blocked... default safety filters can occasionally block such content, biasing the measurement. ... This only affects the *target* model's freedom to express distress, not anything harmful.
